convoLines.text: "...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Omar. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing. Just... be straight with me."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"Mine's Columbus, Ohio, I think — heat on pavement, someone's hand huge around mine. Or I invented it. First memories are half real and half the story you needed. Funny how that works."
"Still on your first memory. — or so they tell me."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Silas always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"What's this about? Honest. I can work with honest."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Still on your plan here. Life's funny that way."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? I've said enough."
"Silas owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I check the treeline every hour. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What's something from your old life that's actually useful here?"
"...Not dumb at all. The people who can't wait are the ones who make mistakes. You're an asset."
"Being a tailor taught me to read people fast — who's lying, who's scared, who needs a job. Turns out that's a survival skill. Who knew…"
"Still on your useful old-life skills."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"That's not — that's not what happened." Lucia's hands won't stop moving. "You're twisting things."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Okay. That's — I need a minute. A long minute."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
LaToya shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Nora. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me about that kitchen — morning light, three years old. Have any other memories come back since?"
They nod. "Okay."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Have you heard what they're calling Hummice? LaToya is pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They take that in without interrupting.
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Roberto grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Roberto is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what they confided — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. LaToya doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Omar. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
Found something. Follow it to the moot.
Said. At the moot. Let the fire decide what it means.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? That's the priority."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took LaToya — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Roberto is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"You said patience was your old-life superpower — really waiting, without fidgeting. Still your answer?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"Okay." Lucia looks down. "Okay. It was me. 1× Plant fiber — I was hungry and I... I'm sorry." Their voice is small.
"Still on that personal stuff. We all learn."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Silas Murray is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Silas kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: Layla picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Ritual & Meaning (Level 1). Marking the dead matters. Even without religion, ritual holds grief.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Silas Murray, 6 days. The mantle passes to Layla Mansour.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Layla Mansour, 44 — a tattoo artist. Her hands know different work now: Green Whisper.

lastSay: d30: Roberto traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
d30: 🍽️ Isadora leaves the foraging basket at the door. "The pantry can't take more — sitting with the elders instead."
d30: 🍽️ Aki watches another basket arrive and laughs. "We're feeding the shelves more than ourselves. Not today."
d31: — DAY 31 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d31: Dawn. You wake rested. (+3 health, energy restored. Your sleeping body burned less — 78 kcal conserved. By the fire. Good enough.)
